justifications.clinical.clinicalOutcomes: RCT evidence supports CBIT efficacy for tic reduction; OT-specific certification outcomes not studied.
justifications.clinical.efficiency: 2-day CBIT workshop; moderate cost; training is accessible for OT and psychology providers.
justifications.clinical.caseloadApplicability: Applicable to the narrow population with tic disorders and Tourette syndrome; very limited scope.
justifications.clinical.reimbursement: Limited commercial coverage for behavioral tic intervention; mostly self-pay or EAP; no dedicated CPT code.
justifications.clinical.marketDemand: Limited employer demand; niche behavioral intervention for specific OT and behavioral health roles.
justifications.clinical.patientSatisfaction: Tic reduction has substantial QoL impact for patients and families.
justifications.business.cashPayViability: Tourette families actively pay cash — CBIT-trained providers are scarce and waitlists are long.
justifications.business.pricingLeverage: Scarcity + motivated families supports premium per-session and intensive-package pricing.
justifications.business.marketDifferentiation: Few OTs/psychologists are CBIT-trained; Tourette Association directory drives direct referrals.
justifications.business.ownerLeverage: Trainable protocol — additional clinicians can be brought up to deliver under the brand.
justifications.business.marketDemand: Strong demand within the Tourette community, though general consumer awareness is modest.
justifications.business.efficiency: TAA training is relatively short and affordable for the revenue it unlocks.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyRecognition: Not a board specialty; recognized as a niche skill but doesn't carry weight in OT promotion files alone.
justifications.academicClinical.scholarship: Active CBIT research literature, though most authors are psychology/psychiatry rather than OT faculty.
justifications.academicClinical.teachingValue: Adds depth to pediatric/mental-health OT content but isn't core curriculum.
justifications.academicClinical.evidenceDepth: Strong RCT support — first-line behavioral treatment for tic disorders.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyDemand: Rarely listed in OT faculty postings.
justifications.academicClinical.efficiency: Quick and inexpensive to obtain relative to the clinical credibility it provides.
